Nepal's Community Forestry program is globally recognized as one of the most successful participatory conservation models: 22,000+ Community Forest User Groups (CFUGs) manage 2.2 million hectares (40% of Nepal's forests) with locally elected governing committees. Nepal's forest cover has increased from 26% (1990s) to 44% (2020s) — a reversal of deforestation through community management. CFUGs sell forest products and use revenues for community development. Nepal's biodiversity includes 8 of 10 highest peaks, 500+ bird species (including rare birds of Annapurna), Red Panda (endemic), Bengal Tiger, and Snow Leopard.
laws.penalty: Commercial logging without permit: up to 5 years. Poaching Red Panda or Snow Leopard: up to 15 years. Illegal trade in timber: forest officer confiscation and criminal prosecution. Setting forest fires: up to 5 years.
exceptions: Community Forest User Groups may harvest designated forest products under management plan
Buffer zone communities around national parks may collect firewood and grasses under quota system
Individual households may use fallen dead wood for cooking fuel without permit
laws.sourceLabel: Department of Forests and Soil Conservation Nepal

quiz.q: What happened to Nepal's forest cover as a result of community forestry, and why is this unusual?
options: Nepal's forest cover decreased from 50% to 30% due to population pressure
Nepal's forest cover increased from 26% to 44% through community management — reversing deforestation in a poor, densely populated developing country
Nepal's forests are unchanged — community forestry only prevents deforestation
Nepal's reforestation was entirely funded by foreign donors with no community participation
quiz.explanation: Nepal's forest cover increase from approximately 26% (1990s) to 44% (2020s) is remarkable: most developing countries with Nepal's population density and poverty levels experience forest loss. The difference is Nepal's Community Forestry program (22,000+ CFUGs) where local communities own forest management rights, sell products, and directly benefit from forest health. When communities profit from forest products, they protect forests from encroachment and fire. Nepal's experience demonstrates that community tenure over forests can reverse deforestation — a lesson increasingly applied globally in climate forest conservation.

laws.title: Nepal-India Open Border Treaty & Migration
laws.subtitle: The world's most open bilateral border policy
laws.fullDescription: Nepal and India maintain one of the world's most open bilateral borders under the Treaty of Peace and Friendship 1950: Nepali and Indian nationals may freely move, live, work, and own property in each other's countries without visas or work permits. This open border supports enormous population movements: 3-4 million Nepalis live and work in India at any time; millions of Indians work in Nepal's lowlands. The Gurkha tradition — Nepali soldiers serving in Indian Army and British Army — is a legacy of colonial and post-colonial military relationships. Nepal's lowland (Madhesi) communities have ethnically similar populations on the Indian (Bihar, Uttar Pradesh) side — creating complex cross-border family ties.
laws.penalty: Passport forgery or travel document fraud: up to 7 years. Arms smuggling across India-Nepal border: up to life. Human trafficking across open border: up to 20 years (open border does not legalize trafficking).
exceptions: No visa required for Nepali-Indian bilateral movement under 1950 Treaty
Both countries' nationals may work and own property with same rights as citizens in each other's country
Citizens of third countries using Nepal-India border must have appropriate visas — the open border privilege applies only to Nepali and Indian nationals

quiz.q: What unique bilateral agreement makes the India-Nepal border special?
options: India and Nepal have the world's most heavily militarized border with 100,000 troops
The 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship allows free movement, work, and property ownership for both countries' nationals — one of the world's most open bilateral border arrangements
India and Nepal have no formal border — the boundary is completely unmarked
Nepal and India's border is open only to Buddhist pilgrims traveling to Lumbini
quiz.explanation: The India-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship (1950) is extraordinary: citizens of either country may freely enter, reside, own property, and work in the other country without any permit or visa. No other two sovereign countries in the world have this level of open movement rights. The result: 3-4 million Nepalis work in India at any time, contributing remittances home; millions of Indians live in Nepal's Terai. This open border creates deep economic interdependence — and is also used by traffickers and smugglers, requiring security cooperation despite the openness.

laws.title: Earthquake Disaster Response — Nepal 2015 and Health System
laws.subtitle: Post-earthquake reconstruction and health system resilience
laws.fullDescription: Nepal's 2015 Gorkha earthquake (7.8 magnitude, April 25) and its aftershocks killed 9,000 people, injured 23,000, and destroyed 500,000 houses — concentrated in mountain districts including ancient Kathmandu Valley heritage sites. The health system response: major hospitals in Kathmandu were damaged, triggering international field hospital deployments. Nepal's constitution (2015) was adopted after the earthquake amid displaced populations — a remarkable governance achievement. Post-earthquake reconstruction was slow and controversial: foreign aid ($4B pledged) was partially misused or delayed; reconstruction authority faced corruption allegations. Nepal's National Reconstruction Authority (2015-2021) closed, with reconstruction 80% complete. Earthquake preparedness remains critical for Kathmandu Valley (estimated 40,000 casualties possible in future 8.0 event).
laws.penalty: Substandard construction not meeting earthquake-resistant building codes: administrative penalties and demolition. Misuse of earthquake reconstruction funds: criminal prosecution under CIAA. Operating damaged unreinforced building after unsafe notice: administrative closure.
exceptions: Heritage site reconstruction requires special UNESCO collaboration permits with different engineering standards
Emergency temporary shelters may be constructed without full building permit during declared disaster period
Community reconstruction of rural homes under Owner-Driven program has simplified earthquake-resistant design specifications

quiz.q: What governance achievement occurred in Nepal while earthquake reconstruction was underway?
options: Nepal cancelled all democratic elections due to the earthquake
Nepal adopted its new constitution (2015) — transitioning from Hindu Kingdom to federal secular republic — while simultaneously managing post-earthquake reconstruction
Nepal's government collapsed after the earthquake and was replaced by military rule
Nepal merged with India for earthquake recovery assistance
quiz.explanation: Nepal adopted its landmark 2015 Constitution on September 20, 2015 — less than 5 months after the catastrophic April 25 earthquake that killed 9,000 people. The Constituent Assembly (elected in 2013) finalized the constitution while managing a national disaster, with some Assembly sessions conducted in temporary facilities. The constitution transformed Nepal from a unitary state to a federal republic with 7 provinces. Completing the constitutional transition while managing earthquake recovery, refugee returns, and international aid coordination was a remarkable governance feat — though the constitution itself later sparked Madhesi protests over representation.
